# Button component

Import `TngButtonComponent` into the consuming standalone component:

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { TngButtonComponent } from '@tailng-ui/components';

@Component({
  standalone: true,
  imports: [TngButtonComponent],
  template: `
    <tng-button tone="primary" appearance="solid" type="button" (click)="save()">
      Save changes
    </tng-button>
  `,
})
export class SaveButtonExample {
  save(): void {}
}
```

Public inputs include:

- `appearance`: `ghost | outline | solid`; default `solid`.
- `tone`: `danger | neutral | primary | success`; default `primary`.
- `size`: `lg | md | sm`; default `md`.
- `type`: native button type; default `button`.
- `disabled`: boolean.
- `ariaLabel`, `ariaLabelledby`, `ariaControls`, `ariaExpanded`, `ariaHasPopup`, and `ariaPressed`.

Prefer visible button text. Use `ariaLabel` for an icon-only button.

# Dialog component

`TngDialogComponent` supplies the modal panel, backdrop, focus management, escape handling, scroll locking, and focus restoration.

```ts
import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { TngDialogComponent } from '@tailng-ui/components';

@Component({
  standalone: true,
  imports: [TngDialogComponent],
  template: `
    <button type="button" (click)="open.set(true)">Open review</button>

    <tng-dialog
      title="Review changes"
      description="Confirm before publishing the release."
      [open]="open()"
      (openChange)="open.set($event)"
    >
      <p>Review the pending changes.</p>
      <button type="button" (click)="open.set(false)">Cancel</button>
    </tng-dialog>
  `,
})
export class ReviewDialogExample {
  readonly open = signal(false);
}
```

Inputs:

- `open`: dialog visibility.
- `title`: accessible title; default `Dialog`.
- `description`: optional accessible description.
- `closeOnBackdrop`: default `true`.
- `closeOnEscape`: default `true`.

Outputs:

- `openChange`: synchronize external visibility state.
- `closed`: close reason: `backdrop`, `close-button`, `escape`, or `programmatic`.

# TailNG components

TailNG components are standalone Angular components exported from `@tailng-ui/components`.

Detailed agent guides currently cover:

- [Button](https://tailng.dev/ai/components/button/overview.md)
- [Input](https://tailng.dev/ai/components/input/overview.md)
- [Dialog](https://tailng.dev/ai/components/dialog/overview.md)
- [Table](https://tailng.dev/ai/components/table/overview.md)

For every component:

1. Import the component class into the consuming standalone Angular component.
2. Use the documented selector and public inputs.
3. Load the TailNG theme contract stylesheet.
4. Provide an accessible name where the component does not have visible labelling.
5. Run the Angular production build after integration.

The absence of an agent guide does not imply that a component does not exist. Consult the [human component catalog](https://tailng.dev/components) and verify exports in the installed package before use.

# Input component

Use `TngInputComponent` for the styled wrapper:

```ts
import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { TngInputComponent } from '@tailng-ui/components';

@Component({
  standalone: true,
  imports: [TngInputComponent],
  template: `
    <tng-input
      type="email"
      placeholder="team@example.com"
      ariaLabel="Work email"
      autocomplete="email"
      [value]="email()"
      (valueChange)="email.set($event)"
    />
  `,
})
export class EmailInputExample {
  readonly email = signal<string | null>(null);
}
```

The component supports native-style attributes including `type`, `placeholder`, `autocomplete`, `required`, `readonly`, `disabled`, `min`, `max`, `minlength`, `maxlength`, `pattern`, and input events.

Use `ariaLabel` when no visible label is associated with the field. Use `ariaErrormessage` and `ariaInvalid` for validation feedback. For projected prefixes or suffixes, use `TngInputFieldComponent` with the relevant primitives.

# Table component

Define typed column metadata and row data:

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { TngTableComponent, type TngTableColumn } from '@tailng-ui/components';

type ReleaseRow = Readonly<{ service: string; owner: string; status: string }>;

@Component({
  standalone: true,
  imports: [TngTableComponent],
  template: `
    <tng-table
      ariaLabel="Release status"
      density="compact"
      stickyHeader
      [columns]="columns"
      [items]="rows"
    />
  `,
})
export class ReleaseStatusTableExample {
  readonly columns: readonly TngTableColumn<ReleaseRow>[] = [
    { id: 'service', label: 'Service', sortable: true },
    { id: 'owner', label: 'Owner' },
    { id: 'status', label: 'Status' },
  ];

  readonly rows: readonly ReleaseRow[] = [
    { service: 'Billing API', owner: 'Mina Lee', status: 'Ready' },
    { service: 'Search index', owner: 'Omar Aziz', status: 'Blocked' },
  ];
}
```

Provide `ariaLabel` or `ariaLabelledby`. Column IDs default to property lookup when no accessor is provided. Use meaningful column labels because sortable headers announce them.

The component also supports density, sticky headers, sorting state, filtering state, pagination state, loading/error states, row styling, nested column groups, and custom cell/header templates.

# TailNG configuration

For a standalone Angular application:

1. Configure the runtime theme provider with [standalone Angular configuration](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/standalone-angular.md).
2. Choose exactly one styling setup:
   - [Plain CSS](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/plain-css.md)
   - [Tailwind CSS](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/tailwind.md)
3. Configure [icons](https://tailng.dev/ai/icons/index.md) only when the application uses `tng-icon` or components that require registered icons.
4. Import each standalone TailNG component in the Angular component that uses it.

# Plain CSS configuration

Import the published theme stylesheet once in `src/styles.css`:

```css
@import '@tailng-ui/theme/index.css';
```

The root stylesheet imports the complete component-contract bundle. To load contracts without the root entry point, use:

```css
@import '@tailng-ui/theme/component-contracts/index.css';
```

Override semantic variables after the import:

```css
:root {
  --tng-semantic-background-canvas: #ffffff;
  --tng-semantic-background-surface: #f8fafc;
  --tng-semantic-foreground-primary: #0f172a;
  --tng-semantic-border-subtle: #cbd5e1;
  --tng-semantic-accent-brand: #2563eb;
  --tng-semantic-focus-ring: rgb(37 99 235 / 35%);
}
```

Do not reference `@tailng-ui/theme/css`; that is not a published package export in the current package manifest.

# Standalone Angular configuration

Register the TailNG theme provider once near the application root:

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { provideRouter } from '@angular/router';
import { defaultDarkThemePreset, provideTailngTheme } from '@tailng-ui/theme';

import { routes } from './app.routes';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideRouter(routes), provideTailngTheme({ theme: defaultDarkThemePreset })],
};
```

`provideTailngTheme` applies the selected theme through TailNG's Angular adapter. Import it from `@tailng-ui/theme`; do not use an invented `provideTheme` helper.

Configure icon providers separately when required.

# Tailwind CSS configuration

Install Tailwind for the version used by the application. TailNG's current documentation uses Tailwind 3 configuration:

```bash
pnpm add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
```

Configure template discovery and disable Tailwind preflight when the application owns reset behavior:

```ts
import type { Config } from 'tailwindcss';

export default {
  content: ['./src/**/*.{html,ts}'],
  corePlugins: {
    preflight: false,
  },
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        brand: 'var(--tng-semantic-accent-brand)',
      },
    },
  },
  plugins: [],
} satisfies Config;
```

Load utilities and TailNG contracts from `src/styles.css`:

```css
@layer tw.preflight, components, tng.tokens, tng.contracts, utilities;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;

@import '@tailng-ui/theme/component-contracts/index.css';
```

Keep component behavior and semantic contract variables in TailNG; use Tailwind utilities for application-owned layout and presentation.

# TailNG icons

Install the package:

```bash
pnpm add @tailng-ui/icons
```

Register the built-in Lucide pack:

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { provideTngIcons } from '@tailng-ui/icons';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideTngIcons()],
};
```

Import and use the standalone component:

```ts
import { TngIcon } from '@tailng-ui/icons';
```

```html
<!-- Decorative when adjacent text provides the meaning. -->
<tng-icon icon="home" size="1.25rem" />

<!-- Meaningful standalone icon. -->
<tng-icon icon="search" label="Search" size="1.25rem" />
```

Unprefixed names use the default pack. Explicit references use `pack:name`, for example `lucide:star`.

Use `@tailng-ui/icons/core` when the application should register only explicitly imported icons and exclude the built-in registry. In that mode, provide at least one pack to `provideTngIcons`.

# TailNG agent guide

Use this documentation when creating or modifying an Angular application with TailNG.

## Required workflow

1. Read the [package versions](https://tailng.dev/ai/versions.json).
2. Choose package installation or ownable installation from the [installation guide](https://tailng.dev/ai/installation/index.md).
3. Apply the [Angular configuration](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/index.md).
4. Import only the components used by the application.
5. Configure [theme](https://tailng.dev/ai/theme/index.md) and [icons](https://tailng.dev/ai/icons/index.md) when required.
6. Run the application's production build and fix integration errors before adding more UI.

Do not guess package names, exports, selectors, providers, or CSS entry points. Use the documents in the machine-readable [index](https://tailng.dev/ai/index.json).

---

Source: https://tailng.dev/ai/installation/index.md

# TailNG installation

TailNG supports two adoption paths.

## Package installation

Use published packages when the application should receive TailNG fixes through dependency upgrades. Start with [package installation](https://tailng.dev/ai/installation/packages.md).

## Ownable installation

Use the `tailng` CLI when the application should copy component source into the application for local ownership and customization. Start with [ownable installation](https://tailng.dev/ai/installation/ownable.md).

Do not mix the two paths for the same component without a deliberate migration plan. After either path, run the application's production build.

---

Source: https://tailng.dev/ai/installation/new-angular-project.md

# New Angular project

Create a standalone application with routing and CSS:

```bash
ng new tailng-app --standalone --routing --style css
cd tailng-app
```

Install TailNG:

```bash
pnpm add @tailng-ui/components @tailng-ui/primitives @tailng-ui/cdk @tailng-ui/theme @tailng-ui/icons
```

Then:

1. Configure the theme provider using the [standalone Angular guide](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/standalone-angular.md).
2. Import the TailNG stylesheet using the [plain CSS guide](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/plain-css.md).
3. Add the required standalone component imports.
4. Run `ng build` or the project's production build command.

Do not continue to feature development while Angular reports missing peer dependencies, unknown TailNG elements, or unresolved CSS imports.

# Ownable installation

List the components supported by the installed CLI version:

```bash
pnpm dlx tailng list
```

Preview an installation:

```bash
pnpm dlx tailng add button --dry-run
```

Install into the current Angular application:

```bash
pnpm dlx tailng add button
```

Use `--cwd <path>` when the Angular application is not the current directory. Generated source is written below `src/app/tailng-ui/<component>/`.

Do not overwrite existing generated files unless the user explicitly wants replacement. The CLI rejects existing files by default; `--force` opts into overwrite behavior.

After generation, follow the CLI's import hints and run the application build.

# Package installation

Check [versions.json](https://tailng.dev/ai/versions.json) before installation. The component package declares its supported Angular range and its TailNG peer dependencies there.

## Styled components with theme and icons

```bash
pnpm add @tailng-ui/components @tailng-ui/primitives @tailng-ui/cdk @tailng-ui/theme @tailng-ui/icons
```

```bash
npm install @tailng-ui/components @tailng-ui/primitives @tailng-ui/cdk @tailng-ui/theme @tailng-ui/icons
```

```bash
yarn add @tailng-ui/components @tailng-ui/primitives @tailng-ui/cdk @tailng-ui/theme @tailng-ui/icons
```

`@tailng-ui/components` ships separately from `@tailng-ui/primitives` and `@tailng-ui/cdk`; install those packages explicitly.

Next, apply the [standalone Angular configuration](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/standalone-angular.md), then choose [plain CSS](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/plain-css.md) or [Tailwind CSS](https://tailng.dev/ai/configuration/tailwind.md).

# TailNG theme

The theme package has two complementary responsibilities:

- Runtime theme definitions and presets through `provideTailngTheme`.
- Component styling contracts through published CSS.

Most styled applications need both:

```ts
provideTailngTheme({ theme: defaultDarkThemePreset });
```

```css
@import '@tailng-ui/theme/index.css';
```

Read [runtime themes](https://tailng.dev/ai/theme/runtime.md) for preset application and [theme tokens](https://tailng.dev/ai/theme/tokens.md) for CSS customization.

---

Source: https://tailng.dev/ai/theme/runtime.md

# Runtime themes

Apply a preset in `app.config.ts`:

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { defaultThemePreset, provideTailngTheme } from '@tailng-ui/theme';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideTailngTheme({ theme: defaultThemePreset })],
};
```

Built-in exports include default, minimal, slate, nexus, prism, atlas, sterling, and daybook-classic presets, with light and dark variants where exported by the package.

Use `createTheme` or `mergeTheme` for programmatic theme composition. Use `toCssVars` when CSS variable output is needed outside the Angular provider.

---

Source: https://tailng.dev/ai/theme/tokens.md

# Theme tokens and contracts

Import the full component contract bundle:

```css
@import '@tailng-ui/theme/component-contracts/index.css';
```

Override shared control variables on `:root`, a theme scope, or a component subtree:

```css
:root {
  --tng-control-bg: var(--tng-semantic-background-surface);
  --tng-control-fg: var(--tng-semantic-foreground-primary);
  --tng-control-border: var(--tng-semantic-border-strong);
  --tng-control-radius: 0.5rem;
  --tng-focus-ring-color: var(--tng-semantic-focus-ring);
}
```

Prefer semantic and shared contract variables over selectors that depend on internal component markup. Scope an override to a component subtree when the change should not affect the whole application.

# TailNG troubleshooting

## Unknown TailNG element

Confirm that the corresponding standalone component is present in the consuming component's `imports` array. Import it from the documented package root.

## Components render without expected styling

Confirm that `src/styles.css` imports `@tailng-ui/theme/index.css` or the required component-contract stylesheet. Verify that the CSS import resolves during the production build.

## Missing theme provider

Register `provideTailngTheme` once in the root `ApplicationConfig`. Do not substitute an undocumented provider name.

## Icon is empty or unresolved

Register `provideTngIcons()` and verify the icon name. When using `@tailng-ui/icons/core`, provide explicit packs.

## Dependency resolution fails

Read [versions.json](https://tailng.dev/ai/versions.json) and compare the installed Angular and TailNG packages with the published peer ranges. Install `@tailng-ui/primitives` and `@tailng-ui/cdk` explicitly with `@tailng-ui/components`.

## Ownable installation refuses to write

Use `--dry-run` first. Existing files are protected by default. Use `--force` only when overwriting is intended.
